The #CoilyCurly hashtag celebrates natural hair textures between curly and coily, with content focused on haircare tips and styling.

Recent findings suggest that products that combine hydration, targeted care and sensory experiences are ruling the bodycare category. Hydrating body mists meet demand for lightweight, water-like moisturizers that deliver lotion-level hydration, while anti-sweat hand creams offer targeted solutions for managing perspiration on the hands. Growing demand for hand mists suggest interest in convenient, fragrant formats that refresh and sanitize on the go, while niacinamide body wash is an example of products designed to support the skin’s moisture barrier. Finally, strawberry body scrub reflects demand for fruit-inspired bodycare that combines exfoliation with appealing scents and ingredients.

Across bodycare brands, there’s growing interest in those offering specialized and efficient approaches to personal care and grooming. Carpe reflects demand for clinical-strength sweat and odor control, while Hanni highlights simplified bodycare through “skip-step” essentials, with a particular rise in searches for its Splash Salve in-shower body balm. Proraso stands out for its Italian men’s grooming heritage. Estée Lauder has evolved its fragrance range by incorporating bodycare into its iconic scent collections, as searches for its Beautiful Perfumed Body Powder grow. Meanwhile, Prequel reflects interest in dermatologist-developed, science-backed skincare centered on skin barrier health.

In a recent development, this week on TikTok, the #DiscountMakeup hashtag is flooded with shoppers unexpectedly discovering Jeffree Star Cosmetics products at Dollar Tree. Meanwhile, content around #PerfumeMists is focused on reviews and recommendations of lightweight, refreshing fragrance formats. #TattooLipLiner content is also on the rise, featuring ink-like liners, peel-off stains, and semi-permanent lip treatments for long-lasting lip definition. #GlowyMakeupRoutine points to interest in luminous, radiant makeup looks and routines, while #FeatheredHair highlights interest in the ’70s voluminous, heavily layered hair look. Together, these trends highlight how beauty content is increasingly shaped by product discovery, makeup routines and nostalgic aesthetics.

Recent findings suggest that there’s growing interest in fragrance trends that combine personalization, identity, and convenience. Alcohol-free fragrances, for example, reflect demand for alternative formulations to traditional perfumes, while custom perfumes point to interest in personalized scents tailored to individual preferences. The rise of masculine fragrances suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male and female consumers alike, while gothic perfume reflects demand for darker and more mysterious aromatic profiles that evoke the romantic and atmospheric elements of the goth aesthetic. Finally, travel fragrances, the portable and convenient scent formats designed to make fragrance easier to pack and use on the go, are also trending.

Sources indicate that this month, there’s particular interest in fragrance brands offering distinctive approaches to scent. Lore’s emotive, transportive fragrances translate specific moods and places into immersive scent experiences, while MCM Fragrance and Miu Miu highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend recognizable fashion identities into fragrance, with searches for the latter mainly associated with Miutine and its youthful fragrance identity. Ranger Station stands out for its bold, high-concentration, nature-inspired scents, while Maison d’Etto offers perfumes rooted in equestrian influence, contemporary art and architecture. These brands highlight growing consumer interest in fragrance that goes beyond scent itself, offering distinctive stories, identities and sensory experiences.

In a recent development, as we enter October season, #SpookyNailArt is trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in Halloween-inspired nail designs based on playful motifs. Meanwhile, growing interest in the #MakeupColorTheory reinforces the rise of consumers learning about the hues that enhance their features. #ConcertHair highlights demand for hairstyles that are durable, creative and highly accessorized, specifically designed to last throughout a concert, while the #RomanticUpdo reflects interest in soft, feminine hairstyles and intentionally undone styles. #CologneHaul shows interest in discovering and showcasing fragrance purchases and collections.

When it comes to nails, there’s a growing interest in trends that combine precision, personalization, and visually distinct finishes. The Italian manicure, which creates the appearance of longer slender nails, reflects demand for more precise techniques, while nail art pens and letters on nails point to interest in customized designs and intricate details. The rise of glass nail polish highlights a preference for glossy, translucent finishes, and vibrant nails reflect demand for bold, eye-catching colors.

It has been revealed that among this month’s trending nail brands, there’s a clear preference for distinct approaches to at-home manicures. Reusable, press-on nail line Never Have I Ever incorporates licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons into nail designs, while Double Rhythm reinforces interest in accessible, soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies for DIY and salon-style looks. IPolish stands out for its digital color-changing press-on nails, allowing owners to switch between hundreds of shades using a smartphone and activation wand. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, while Sparkle & Co. specializes in DIY dip powders with unique glitters, foils, flakes, glow-in-the-dark, and color-changing effects.

TikTok is seeing an influx of content featuring #BumperBangs, reflecting interest in vintage 1940s and ’50s fringe styles consisting of a bold, rounded shape. Meanwhile, the rise of #CurlyHairBride highlights demand for bridal hair inspiration that embraces natural curls and textured styles. #WigsOnTikTok shows the growing role of TikTok in discovering, styling, and showcasing wigs. #UltaFragrance and #SephoraBeautyAdvisor highlight interest in beauty advisors sharing recommendations, product expertise and customer interactions at retailers Ulta and Sephora. Together, these hashtags highlight interest in vintage looks, occasion-specific styling, and behind-the-scenes beauty retail experiences.

There’s a growing interest in makeup products that combine ease of use, enhanced appearance, and convenient beauty benefits, according to monthly search data. Growth in creamy lip liners points to demand for smooth, easy-to-apply products that shape and define the lips, while lip volumizers help create the appearance of fuller, smoother lips without invasive treatments. Rose gold eyeshadow is also trending, driven by demand for warm, luminous shades. Gripping primer, which is a gel-based product with a tacky finish to hold your makeup in place, reflects interest in creating durable makeup looks that last throughout the day. The rise of SPF face powder reveals interest in facial sun protection beyond conventional sunscreens, with multifunctional products that both protect and control shine.

Across makeup brands, those offering distinctive products spanning various price points are performing particularly well. Hung Vanngo Beauty reflects demand for makeup artist expertise, while Burberry Beauty signals continued interest in luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses. C-beauty brand Cheeryep and Sleek Makeup highlight demand for vibrant, high-pigment makeup and innovative finishes. Maven Beauty, Fashion Nova’s makeup brand, suggests growing demand for affordable beauty options.

On TikTok, #UVHairExtensions are gaining traction, reflecting interest in innovative UV and LED hair extension techniques offering fast application, while #BrownRedHair highlights demand for rich, warm hair color combinations of brown, red, copper, and mahogany tones. Manicurist content featuring #PracticeNails highlights past designs and their training progress, while #CottagecoreNails spotlights whimsical, nature-inspired manicures influenced by cottagecore aesthetics. The rise of #BridesmaidsMakeup reflects growing demand for beauty inspiration tailored to bridesmaids and wedding looks.

Sources indicate that in skincare, monthly interest in products and treatments that combine targeted skin health benefits with gentle, barrier-supporting ingredients and advanced technologies is rising. Silicone-free sunscreen and its lightweight, ingredient-conscious sun protection is trending, while the retinol sandwich method, where retinol is layered between moisturizer to reduce the risk of irritation, is gaining traction among those looking to safely introduce retinol into their routines. There is continued demand for hyaluronic acid face lotions offering convenient, hydrating properties that support moisture retention and skin plumpness, while ceramide toners are designed to strengthen and maintain the skin barrier. Interest in high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) treatments highlights demand for advanced, non-invasive aesthetic treatments focused on skin tightening and rejuvenation.

It has been revealed that for brands, those offering science-backed and targeted skincare solutions are trending. Elm Biosciences, which develops clinical skincare focused on healthy aging and cellular-level care, is gaining traction, while Magic Molecule offers hypochlorous acid solutions that cleanse, reduce inflammation and support skin healing. The rise of TropicSport signals demand for high-performance sun protection during active lifestyles. NewGel+ reflects interest in specialized scarcare and skin repair. The Body Shop, particularly its Drops of Youth line, highlights demand for products targeting early signs of aging while supporting skin resilience against daily environmental stressors.

In a recent development, on TikTok, #SheinMakeupHaul is trending, reflective of the growing interest in discovering and sharing affordable makeup products through beauty hauls. #BestHairOils indicates how more consumers are comparing different hair oils and seeking product recommendations. #BakedBlush features content spotlighting latest blush introduces and shades comparisons through product swatches and reviews. #TinselBraids and #CakeNails highlight playful approaches to self-expression through decorative hairstyles and creative nail designs, with consumers exploring visually distinctive looks.

Industry observers note that this month’s search data highlights growing interest in haircare products that combine targeted follicle growth with plant-based ingredients. Popular hair serums range from including specific active ingredients, with searches for redensyl and peptide serums that help reduce shedding by supporting follicle health and improving fullness, to concern-specific searches such as hair thinning serum. Rice water hairspray highlights demand for convenient, multifunctional products that can strengthen strands, add shine and reduce frizz, while plant-based shampoos reflect growing interest in products made primarily with vegan and botanical ingredients.

Sources indicate that when it comes to haircare brands, those offering performance-driven, science-backed and premium solutions, in particular, are trending. Labo-H reflects demand for Korean scalpcare and hair loss prevention, while UltraSwim highlights interest in cleansing products designed to remove chlorine, chemical odors, and mineral buildup from hair. Bare Anatomy signals demand for science-backed haircare, addressing specific concerns such as shedding, dandruff, frizz, and damage, while Bvlgari Beauty reflects interest in luxury products combining cleansing and scalpcare with the brand’s signature scents. Meanwhile, Iso Beauty highlights growing interest in solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home.

Over on TikTok, #BabyShowerMakeup reflects interest in soft glam makeup looks tailored specifically for mothers and guests attending baby showers, while #MarchMakeup indicates makeup looks based on the birthday month. #QuickCurls highlights demand for fast and easy hairstyling techniques for curly hair, while #LakeHair reflects interest in solutions to avoid or untangle the messy, textured, and sometimes dry or mineral-coated hair associated with freshwater swimming. #AntioxidantSerum shows dermatologist content discussing skincare products centered around antioxidant benefits and protection from environmental stressors.

Across wellness, monthly search data highlights growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits, convenience, and ease of use. Dopamine patches, for example, reflect demand for wearable solutions associated with mood and focus support, while acupressure wristbands reveal interest in convenient solutions for managing and preventing nausea, particularly concerning travel and motion sickness. Screenless fitness trackers demonstrate growing demand for minimalist wearable technology that passively monitors health and activity data without the distraction of a screen. Men’s fertility supplements signal interest in targeted nutritional support for male reproductive health, while liquid zinc supplements highlight demand for convenient ways to prevent or address zinc deficiency and support immune health.

According to recent reports, for brands, there’s growing interest in those offering targeted, convenient, and science-backed wellness solutions. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, easy-to-consume protein products, while Artemis Tea highlights interest in organic herbal teas and wellness blends rooted in traditional herbalism. Nancy’s Probiotic signals demand for organic cultured foods and probiotic-focused nutrition, while EFX Sports reflects interest in performance supplements such as Kre-Alkalyn creatine, designed to support strength and recovery. The rise of Sparkle Wellness relates to continued interest in collagen supplements targeting skin, hair, nails, and overall vitality.

Over on TikTok, the growing traction for #BridalUpdoStyle reflects interest in polished, occasion-ready hairstyles for weddings and special events. #FauxBrows and #HowToSelfTan highlight different approaches to enhancing everyday beauty, from creating realistic, hair-like brow strokes to achieving an even, natural-looking tan at home. #MakeupPR reflects the influencer culture around receiving and unboxing gifted beauty products, as well as creators sharing their experiences with brands. #MakeupOver35 highlights growing interest in makeup techniques and product recommendations tailored to women over the age of 35.

Sources indicate that in the bodycare space, current search trends highlight growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits and convenience with sensory appeal. Alpha hydroxy (AHA) body lotions and hand exfoliators reflect demand for exfoliating and smoothing products that help remove dead skin cells, dirt, and dry patches. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetics. Epsom salt lotions reflect interest in convenient options for muscle relief and recovery, while kojic acid lotions signal demand for targeted brightening and uneven skin tone care.

Industry observers note that as for bodycare brands, those offering targeted, skin-friendly solutions are gaining traction. QV Skincare reflects demand for sensitive skin and barrier-supportive care, while Naked Bee highlights interest in affordable, natural bodycare options incorporating ingredients such as honey, beeswax, and oatmeal. Derman points to demand for targeted antifungal treatments, and Curology reflects growing interest in dermatologist-designed solutions for body breakouts and rough texture. Meanwhile, Luna Daily highlights demand for pH-balanced, microbiome-friendly care for both the body and intimate areas. These brands reveal how the category is evolving through specialist treatments based on body area and skin concern, spanning natural-based products to dermatologist-designed solutions.

Over on TikTok, #VampNails reflect interest in bold, dramatic nail looks inspired by dark and vampy aesthetics. #RootRetouch and #GrayGrowOut highlight different approaches to managing hair color, from concealing visible roots to embracing the transition to natural gray. #HairVolumeHacks signals demand for accessible styling techniques that create fuller, more voluminous hair. #MakeupTrial reflects interest in testing and refining makeup looks ahead of weddings and special events.

This month’s search data highlights a shift toward more occasion-driven and emotionally evocative fragrance choices. The rise of wedding fragrances reflects growing interest in scents associated with meaningful celebrations and special occasions. Sport fragrances signal demand for fresh, energetic scents suited to active lifestyles and everyday wear, while sweet fragrances highlight continued preference for gourmand and indulgent scent profiles, with birthday cake perfume, for example, also offering a familiar scent evocative of childhood memories. Electric perfume, meanwhile, with searches mainly associated with the iconic Revlon fragrance from the 80s, Electric Youth, reflects the enduring appeal of discontinued scents that offer a new form of nostalgia.

When it comes to brands, DefineMe Creative Studio highlights growing interest in fragrance rooted in pop culture, with collaborations such as Barbie connecting scent with recognizable characters and cultural identities. Lore reflects demand for emotive, transportive fragrances that translate specific moods and places into scent experiences. Miu Miu and MCM Fragrance highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend a recognizable fashion identity into the perfume space, with Miu Miu searches mainly associated with the more youthful and feminine Miutine scent. The rise of Kopari, specifically its fragrance mists, reflects demand for lighter fragrance formats suited to everyday use.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #CreamEyeshadowSticks are trending, as demand rises for convenient, easy-to-apply makeup formats that allow consumers to create smooth, buildable eye looks with minimal effort. #ChunkyHighlights and #NailFoils reflect growing interest in creative beauty techniques that add dimension and visual impact to hair and nails. #UltaHairSalon reflects consumers’ and salon workers’ experiences with hair services in retail stores, highlighting a convenient way to access professional salon expertise. The continued interest in #DrySkinSolutions signals demand for targeted skincare solutions focused on relieving dryness and supporting skin hydration.

Recent findings suggest that there’s been a rise in search data for nail art pens, reflecting growing interest in personalized nail creativity that’s nostalgic and enables consumers to experiment with intricate and customized designs. Liquid tape reflects demand for manicure tools that simplify application while improving precision and creating cleaner, more professional-looking results. Glitter nail polish is another Y2K trend regaining momentum, with continued interest in bold, statement-making finishes that add a dose of playfulness to nail looks. The sustained demand for glass nail polish underscores the role of high-gloss translucent finishes as a more classic aesthetic. Meanwhile, celestial nails signal increasing enthusiasm for imaginative and artistic nail designs inspired by cosmic themes and metallic accents.

It has been revealed that nars, which phased out its nail polish line, is trending in search data, reflecting the enduring appeal of discontinued beauty products when consumers maintain connections with iconic shades and search for color dupes still available on the market. Tonic Polish and Pure Ice, meanwhile, highlight growing interest in expressive nail finishes, such as multichromes, magnetics and holographics, as well as accessible trend-driven shades, glitters and metallics that keep manicures more unique. Beyond polish, Burt’s Bees highlights growing demand for nourishing nailcare solutions, such as cuticle creams that provide hydration while supporting dry and brittle nails. Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

On TikTok, #BrighteningEyeMasks reflect demand for targeted skincare solutions, with consumers using under-eye patches to depuff, hydrate, and reduce the appearance of dark circles. Content featuring #MakeupDisaster and #BadNailsCheck highlights the interest from consumers in beauty mishaps, from makeup products that fail to deliver expected results to manicure disasters and negative salon experiences. #SkincareRitual reflects interest in consistent, personalized skincare routines focused on daily maintenance. #NailTechDayInMyLife reflects interest in behind-the-scenes nail content, with consumers engaging with nail technicians’ routines, creative processes, and the realities of running a nail business. Together, these trends reflect growing consumer interest in authentic beauty experiences and personal routines.

In the makeup space, monthly data highlights growing demand for innovative, personalized, and tech-driven cosmetics. Lipstick printers, associated primarily with YSL Beauty, reflect rising interest in tech-enabled beauty personalization, allowing consumers to create customized lip shades on-demand. Aloe lipstick offers hydrating, soothing properties with pH-reactive formulas that adapt to each wearer’s lips. Soft matte lipstick reflects interest in formulas that deliver a velvety, blurred matte finish without the dryness of traditional matte lipsticks, while terracotta lipstick highlights the popularity of warm, earthy shades that offer a transeasonal beauty look. Meanwhile, ginger mascara signals growing interest in softer, natural-looking eye makeup, with this shade offering a light brown to reddish tint that subtly enhances lashes.

Prestige Cosmetics is among this month’s trending makeup brands, reflecting continued demand for accessible, high-pigment products in a broad range of colors. Hung Vanngo Beauty signals sustained interest in makeup artist-founded brands that deliver professional-quality products based on their expertise. Details by Tati signals demand for creator-led beauty brands centered on luxury makeup tools and elevated application. Black Up is a brand tailored to those looking for inclusive makeup options, offering complexion products specifically developed to enhance deeper skin tones. The enduring appeal of Burberry Beauty, meanwhile, reinforces demand for combining premium formulations with sophisticated, fashion-inspired aesthetics.

It has been revealed that over on TikTok, #FrizzyHairHacks and #GrayHairCare reflect growing demand for targeted hair solutions, as more consumers seek practical techniques and specialized products to manage frizz, improve smoothness, and maintain the health and vibrancy of gray and silver hair. #GoldenHourMakeup highlights demand for warm, radiant beauty looks, from golden-toned eye makeup to sun-kissed complexions with natural luminosity. The rise of the #BlondeRoots hashtag reflects continued interest in blonde hair trends that embrace visible roots, like ghost roots. #FullFaceOfDollarTreeMakeup underscores engagement in affordable beauty experimentation, with consumers creating full-face looks using accessible products.

In the skincare space, there’s growing demand for targeted, science-led solutions. Pore mousse reflects interest in innovative K-beauty cleansing formats that deeply purify and refine the appearance of pores, while silicone scar sticks demonstrate demand for convenient scar care that supports scar recovery and improves the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles. Liquid pimple patches are still rising as the next-generation blemish treatment to combine targeted ingredient delivery with an invisible, flexible finish for everyday wear. Peptide eyelash serum reflects rising interest in peptide-powered formulas that strengthen lashes and promote a fuller, healthier appearance. Meanwhile, increased searches regarding retinoid dermatitis signals the heightened awareness of managing irritation associated with active skincare ingredients.

In a recent development, when it comes to skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed products, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Caire Beauty reflects demand for hormone-aware skincare for women aged 40 to 65-plus, offering science-driven formulas designed to address the visible effects of perimenopause and menopause through advanced hydration and skin-rebuilding technologies.

Recent findings suggest that love From Yours highlights the rise of AI-powered personalized skincare, using skin analysis and lifestyle data to create customized routines tailored to individual needs. Radical Skincare represents continued interest in clinical-strength anti-aging solutions that deliver restorative results while remaining suitable for sensitive and blemish-prone skin. Scarlett Whitening, an Indonesian brand, signals growing demand for accessible, ingredient-focused skincare that combines brightening, hydrating, and acne-targeting actives.

Sources indicate that on TikTok, #GlutenFreeMakeup reflects growing interest in inclusive beauty products that cater to ingredient-conscious consumers and specific lifestyle preferences. #FrenchTwistHairstyle and #ColorMelting reflect growing interest in elevated yet wearable hair looks, with consumers embracing timeless styling techniques alongside dimensional, natural-looking hair color trends. #CreamyEyeliner highlights demand for versatile eye makeup products that offer smooth application, rich pigmentation, and effortless wear. #MorningMakeupRoutine points to consumers seeking efficient, everyday beauty rituals and product recommendations that simplify their routines. Together, these trends reflect growing demand for beauty solutions that balance self-expression, convenience, and performance.

Industry observers note that in the haircare space, there is growing interest in haircare solutions that combine convenience and science-backed ingredients alongside targeted treatments to support hair and scalp health. Convenience is a big factor, with waterless dry shampoo and 6-in-1 shampoo signaling the desire for multifunctional products that simplify hair care routines.

Caffeine hair serum highlights increasing interest in scalp-focused formulations designed to help strengthen hair, reduce shedding, and promote the appearance of fuller, healthier-looking hair. Exosome hair therapy underscores the growing popularity of advanced, science-driven hair restoration technologies, with consumers exploring treatments aimed at supporting scalp health, hair regeneration, and overall hair vitality. Finally, overnight hair serum reflects rising demand for treatments that work while customers sleep, delivering deep hydration, nourishment, and repair to improve hair strength and smoothness by morning.

It has been revealed that these trends can also been seen across the haircare brands spiking interest, with science and ingredients sitting at the forefront. Hair fall, thinning hair and scalp health are key concerns, with Minimalist and South Korean brand Aromatica showing up as trending haircare brands. Iso Beauty highlights interest in haircare solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home, while &Honey underscores the popularity of Japanese hair care brands with formulations inspired by honey-based ingredients catering to consumers seeking hydration, shine, and frizz control. Meanwhile, Wow Skin Science reflects continued demand for plant-based haircare products.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #BadNailsCheck has owners showing manicure disasters, sharing nail art that turned out completely different from the reference photo. In contrast, #DamagedHairSolutions signals users on a “healthy hair journey”, sharing tips, routines, and product recommendations for repairing damaged hair. #DIYBlush reflects the growing appeal of personalized beauty, with creators customizing blush shades. #MotherOfTheBrideMakeup highlights demand for elegant, age-inclusive makeup inspiration for weddings and other special occasions. Meanwhile, technicians and creators are sharing techniques, product recommendations, and behind-the-scenes glimpses of their daily work with #LashArtistOfTikTok.

In a recent development, in the wellness space, there’s a growing interest in supplements and solutions that support long-term health, targeted nutrition, and proactive selfcare. Dopamine patches align with demand for wearable wellness solutions aimed at supporting focus, motivation, mood, and cognitive performance. The rise of menopause support supplements highlights interest in formulations that help manage hormonal changes, with consumers seeking products that address symptoms such as hot flashes, mood fluctuations, sleep quality, and overall wellbeing.

Meanwhile, kimchi supplements mirror continued focus on gut health, as more consumers look for probiotic-rich alternatives inspired by fermented foods to support digestion and microbiome balance. Vitamin B5 supplements lean into essential nutrients that aid the breakdown of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, while supporting skin and heart health. Finally, longevity supplements satisfy a growing focus on healthy aging, with consumers seeking science-backed ingredients and formulations that support cellular health and vitality as part of a preventive approach to wellness.

Sources indicate that when it comes to wellness brands, those spanning targeted delivery formats, science-backed nutrition, and performance-focused solutions are performing the best. Gentle Patch reflects demand for convenient, wearable wellness solutions, while Bioschwartz and Webber Naturals represent continued interest in supplement brands that offer vitamins, minerals, probiotics, and herbal formulations for everyday health. Swolverine signals growing demand for performance nutrition that supports strength and recovery, while Zhou Nutrition reflects interest in holistic supplements that promote energy, immune health, sleep, and healthy aging.

On TikTok, the #SummerGlowMakeup and #BeautyFavs hashtags reflect growing interest in curated beauty routines and product discovery, with consumers seeking seasonal makeup inspiration alongside trusted product recommendations. #GeodeNails lean into a demand for artistic, statement-making nail designs that emphasize creativity and self-expression. #DIYMicroLocsJourney adopts a personal storytelling format, as consumers document their hair journeys, while learning protective hair styling techniques. Meanwhile, #DollarTreeSkincareHaul spotlights affordable skincare products, as consumers explore budget-friendly options that fit into their selfcare routines.

In a recent development, in the bodycare category, there’s growing interest in products that combine targeted treatments, ingredient-focused formulations, and at-home wellness solutions. The rise in searches for cellulite oil suggests that consumers are seeking botanical oil blends and firming formulations designed for massaging into the skin as part of anti-cellulite routines. Grape soap highlights demand for playful, fruit-inspired products that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetic appeal. Meanwhile, the popularity of AHA body lotions signals continued interest in ingredient-led skincare, with consumers seeking exfoliating body creams that improve skin texture and smoothness. Epsom salt lotion and red light therapy panels reflect the growing adoption of at-home recovery and wellness routines, as consumers seek products and devices that support muscle comfort, recovery, skin rejuvenation, and temporary pain relief.

Science-backed brands with plant-based ingredients and luxury positionings are soaring. Hada Labo, a Japanese brand, and QV Skincare reflect continued demand for gentle, hydration-focused products that support healthy skin through barrier-supportive formulations. Just Nutritive signals a consumer preference for handcrafted, botanical-based products that emphasize naturally derived ingredients, while Nordic Goddess points to the growing intersection of wellness and bodycare, as more consumers seek topical solutions that incorporate THC and CBD for targeted relief. Meanwhile, La Mer underscores demand for premium bodycare, combining intensive hydration with a luxurious, sensorial experience.

In a recent development, over on TikTok, #CheetahHair, #HaircutTutorials, and #HairFoils are all trending, reflecting a broader shift toward more experimental and technique-driven approaches to hair styling. #CheetahHair highlights bold, pattern-led hair looks that emphasize self-expression and visual impact, #HaircutTutorials points to the growing demand for accessible, step-by-step education from hair stylists, while #HairFoils underscores continued interest in professional coloring techniques. In addition, #PlaitsBraids highlights the appeal of finished braided styles, with content featuring both at-home and salon-created results for men and women. Meanwhile, #CoconutOilForSkin signals an ongoing interest in multi-purpose ingredients used across selfcare routines. Together, these trends reflect a move toward both skill-based hair experimentation and ingredient-driven selfcare practices.

Luxury fragrances are becoming more than a special occasion spritz. Consumers are investing in scents that have wide appeal, from sport fragrances for energy, freshness, and an active lifestyle, to sweet smells that have a touch of nostalgia.

It has been revealed that tomato perfume underscores the rise of unconventional fragrance notes, reflecting curiosity around earthy and garden-fresh scent experiences that stand apart from traditional or gourmand offerings. Meanwhile, perfume-making kits are becoming increasingly popular, as rising interest in personalization and creativity push consumers to explore DIY fragrance creation and craft scents tailored to their individual preferences.

Riiffs and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect growing consumer demand for accessible fragrances with strong, long-lasting effects and scent profiles that blend Middle Eastern perfumery traditions with modern styles. Pure Instinct and Rahasya signal interest in fragrances that feel more personal and body-driven, where consumers are drawn to scents designed to interact with individual chemistry and enhance perceived personal appeal. Lore reflects demand for more experiential and concept-led fragrances, as consumers increasingly seek scents that go beyond smell to evoke places, moods, and narratives. Meanwhile, Miu Miu highlights the enduring influence of fashion houses within the fragrance category, as consumers continue to seek scents that blend luxury, creativity, and modern self-expression.

Sources indicate that #RedDyedHair, #LashDye, and #SelfTannerHack all reflect a broader shift toward at-home beauty experimentation through DIY techniques. #RedDyedHair highlights bold self-applied color changes as a form of personal expression and transformation. #LashDye reflects interest in low-maintenance beauty routines, where users tint lashes for longer-lasting definition, and #SelfTannerHack shows how shared tips are used to achieve more controlled, even tanning results. Then, #NosePatches and #NeckSkincareRoutine point to growing demand for targeted skincare solutions, with the former focusing on pore care and blackheads for a quick, temporary smoothing effect, while the latter underscores increasing awareness of often-neglected areas that require attention beyond the face. Together, these trends reflect a move into DIY-driven beauty and targeted treatment routines.

When it comes to nails, consumers are seeking designs that blend self-expression, practicality, and care. BB cream nails reflect demand for natural-looking, low-maintenance manicures, while comic nails highlight a desire for creative and expressive nail art. Matcha nails point to the growing traction of soft green tones, influenced by the cult popularity of the beverage, while solid gel nail glue indicates interest in durable, mess-free nail application, as consumers increasingly value long-lasting performance. Crystal nail files reflect a growing awareness of nail health, with consumers seeking gentler tools that help maintain strong, smooth nails and minimize damage.

The rise of The Gelbottle, Nail Reformation, Kleo Kolor, and Curvlife each proves growing demand for long-lasting nail solutions that deliver salon-quality results. The Gelbottle reflects interest in professional-grade systems that strengthen and enhance natural nails, while Nail Reformation and Kleo Kolor point to the popularity of reusable press-ons and durable at-home manicure options. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light. Meanwhile, Hermès underscores the premiumization of the nail category, with consumers seeking luxury nail products and tools featuring shades inspired by Hermès’s design heritage and silk draping — finished with a high-gloss, satin sheen in a single coat.

On TikTok, #CyberPunkNails reflects interest in futuristic nail art that combines punk influences, neon accents, metallic finishes, and bold 3D details. #SkinTintStick highlights demand for hybrid complexion products that offer light coverage with skincare benefits in a portable format. #TCAPeel and #MicrobiomeSkincare signal growing consumer interest in understanding the mechanisms behind skin behavior, from chemical exfoliation and skin renewal to the role of the microbiome in barrier health. In the case of #TCAPeel, viral social media content often emphasizes the risks of extreme at-home use. #HairLossJourney extends this same behavior pattern into haircare, where individuals actively seek to understand the causes of hair loss, sharing progress and seeking support and solutions. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward beauty that combines experimentation, care, and awareness of underlying skin and hair health.

Makeup products and techniques that deliver precision, convenience, and natural-looking results are soaring. Contour stain reflects demand for long-wearing, transfer-resistant sculpting products that provide definition with minimal maintenance throughout the day. Meanwhile, cool-toned blush and cool-toned contour underscore consumers’ increasing focus on shade accuracy. At the same time, ghost and pre-glued lashes highlight demand for effortless lash enhancement, combining natural-looking results with faster and easier application methods. Together, these trends suggest that makeup is evolving toward personalized routines that prioritize subtle enhancement, ease of use, and products tailored to individual features and preferences.

In a recent development, across makeup brands, the rise of Elroel and Purito highlights the continued influence of K-beauty. Elroel reflects growing demand for adaptive complexion products that simplify shade matching, while purito emphasizes lightweight coverage and minimal formulations to avoid skin sensitivities. Dermatologist-founded Rodan and Fields further reinforces interest in hybrid complexion products that combine cosmetic performance with skincare benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of Brow Daddy highlights consumers’ focus on expertly defined brows and professional-grade beauty solutions offering precision and long-lasting results. KJH.Brand, introduced by makeup artist Katie Jane Hughes, underscores the appeal of creative, multi-use makeup that encourages self-expression and flexible application across the eyes, lips, and cheeks.

Sources indicate that as more consumers focus on maintaining hair health and reducing damage, #BedtimeHaircare is trending on TikTok and reflects growing interest in overnight prevention treatments. #CollagenFilm highlights K-beauty innovation in the form of dissolvable collagen films, designed for topical application to deliver instant hydration and a smoother, firmer appearance. #BrowFreeze, meanwhile, reflects continued interest in lifted, feathered brow styling that creates a laminated look. #613AmazonWig signals demand for affordable, pre-lightened platinum blonde wigs that enable bold color experimentation without chemical processing, while #GluelessClosureInstall reflects a broader shift in wig culture toward accessible, low-damage styling, where consumers seek dramatic transformations that are easy to apply, comfortable to wear, and avoid the long-term commitment or potential damage associated with traditional installation methods. Together, these trends reflect a move to beauty routines that balance care and transformation, combining preventative habits with low-damage styling and skin-focused innovation.

Consumers are on the hunt for science-led skincare innovations. Interest in silicone scar sticks reflects demand for effective scar products that support skin recovery and improve the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, while simplifying daily treatment routines. Rising interest in needle patches highlights demand for advanced delivery technologies, which enable active ingredients to be delivered directly for enhanced efficacy and targeted results. PDRN creams and serums tap into regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas associated with skin repair, recovery, and renewal. Meanwhile, growth in matte lip balms highlights a desire for hybrid lip products that bridge skincare and makeup, delivering hydration while providing both a tint and a matte finish.

Among trending skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores the rise in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Wow Skin Science reflects demand for nature-inspired skincare, offering plant-powered formulations free from harsh chemicals. Sincerely Yours highlights the rise of dermatologist-developed skincare tailored to younger consumers, with a focus on barrier support and the unique needs of teenage skin. Isispharma represents the continued strength of dermocosmetic skincare, providing targeted solutions for concerns such as hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and acne through dermatologist-recommended formulations. Sunplay signals growing emphasis on daily sun protection, leveraging advanced Japanese skincare technology to deliver high-performance UV defense.

It has been revealed that on TikTok, #FireHair reflects growing interest in bold, high-impact hair color trends, as more consumers embrace expressive styles. #DyedLocsOnWomen highlights demand for dyed locs as a form of color expression across textured and protective hairstyles. #ShimmerLips leans into the continued interest in glossy, light-reflecting lip finishes, while #WrinkleTreatments underscores rising focus on preventive and corrective skincare solutions, as consumers seek ways to address aging. #HDFrontalWigs showcases high-definition lace frontal wigs, with content centered on installations and styling.

In the haircare space, consumers are searching for products that combine active ingredients, scalp support, and at-home technology. Batana oil shampoos highlight an ongoing interest in nourishing botanical ingredients for hydration and scalpcare, while blonde hair masks emphasize maintenance of tone and softness in color-treated locks. At the same time, red light therapy hats signal the growing adoption of tech-enabled tools for scalp stimulation and hair growth.

Hairburst reflects a growing demand for haircare solutions that support stronger, longer hair and address thinning and breakage. KilgourMD represents a dermatologist-founded, science-backed approach to scalp health, offering a targeted system designed to treat hair thinning through plant-based prevention and care. Tgideas highlights interest in rosemary-based botanical haircare aimed at supporting growth, reducing breakage, and improving scalp health. Dr. Groot reflects the strength of Korean dermatological haircare that zeroes in on scalp balance and hair loss prevention through ingredients such as niacinamide, prebiotics, and probiotics. Trybello signals demand for haircare solutions designed to reduce hair loss and promote thicker, fuller-looking hair.

Sources indicate that on TikTok, #HeatlessStyling reflects rising interest in low-damage hair routines, as consumers seek ways to achieve results without heat tools. #FastHairstyles highlights demand for quick, efficient styling solutions that slot into busy lifestyles while still delivering polished looks. #FaceGlitter signals continued engagement with expressive makeup, focused on bold, playful self-expression. #MonsterHighNails points to the rise of bold, character-inspired nail designs that emphasize individuality and playful aesthetics, especially among Gen Alpha consumers. #NailArtBrush points to the importance of precision tools in nail design, supporting detailed artwork and professional techniques, alongside guidance from nail techs on choosing the best brushes and how to use them effectively.

In a recent development, consumers are increasingly drawn to wellness formats that blend supplementation, wearables, and at-home recovery tools into everyday routines. Alongside these, percussive massage devices highlight the rise of accessible recovery technologies designed to reduce muscle tension and support circulation after exercise. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward personalized wellness routines using multiple formats that prioritize convenience and seamless integration into everyday life.

It has been revealed that javvy Coffee reflects growing demand for functional beverages that integrate wellness benefits such as supporting energy. Myvitamins focuses on simple, accessible nutrition through a wide range of vitamins and supplements that support general health and daily wellbeing. Esther Formula is a South Korean supplement brand known for its glutathione direct films and reflects the rising demand of K-wellness along with beauty-from-within nutrition, where consumers prioritize skin health and radiance through targeted supplementation, along with interest in innovative delivery formats. Swolverine represents performance-focused supplementation designed to support strength, endurance, and recovery through clinically dosed products. Jacob reflects demand for high-protein functional foods made from simple, real ingredients.

#DIYMakeupHacks highlights growing interest in at-home beauty experimentation and resourceful routines, as consumers share and test creative ways to achieve makeup results. #DIYBlush reflects personalization in beauty, with people exploring custom or handmade blush products to tailor color and finish. #SunscreenPowder points to demand for convenience and reapplication-friendly sun protection formats that support on-the-go skincare routines. #NailAcrylic signals focus on durability and design in nailcare, as users compare acrylic applications for strength, longevity, and aesthetic results. #MicroLocInstall reflects interest in protective hairstyling and long-term hair maintenance, particularly around the installation and upkeep of microlocs. Sources indicate that in bodycare, current search trends reveal a strong focus on targeted skin benefits and functional treatment-based products. Sources indicate that ELM Biosciences underscores the growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a “lab-to-patient” approach supporting long-term skin health and the concept of aging well. The surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. Together, these trends reveal a consumer who approaches haircare through targeted, science-backed and ingredient-conscious solutions.

Seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. LED brands like CurrentBody, Shark, Solawave, Vym, Monastery and FAQ have also been leading the charge. Roz sits at the intersection of plant-based sustainability and professional performance delivering botanical-powered results that promote lasting scalp health. This positioning bridges the gap between the accessible, plant-based approach of California Naturals and the salon-quality focus of ISO Beauty — underscoring how consumers increasingly seek conscious formulations alongside visible, high-performance results.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, hashtags like #BraiderOfTikTok and #BridalGlamLook are largely driven by professionals showcasing intricate techniques and polished transformations, suggesting that people turn to the platform for inspiration. It has been revealed that there’s a growing interest in topical, bioactive wellness formats, with patches incorporating GLP-1s and NAD reflecting a shift to skin-applied solutions for metabolic support, longevity, and targeted physiological optimization. Its popularity highlights a broader preference for convenient, flavorful, and results-driven wellness rituals. Collectively, these trends reflect a consumer mindset that blends experimentation with intentionality, seeking measurable benefits through both topical innovation and functional nutrition.

The latest search trends show that consumers are treating wellness as a seamless part of daily life rather than a task. Consumers are increasingly proactive about long-term health, turning to restorative or preventative products like NAD+ and colostrum supplements, as well as personalised wellness rituals and ancient remedies, with magnesium oil and sea moss reflecting a desire for products that are scientifically backed and grounded in tradition. As a result, brands like Transparent Labs and AG1 speak to the demand for science-backed, all-in-one products that simplify health routines while delivering performance and recovery benefits. Armra Colostrum underscores a renewed interest in immunity and gut health, tapping into the appeal of functional ingredients with restorative properties. Parents, meanwhile, are being drawn to Hiya Health for its nutrient-dense offerings designed to support children’s wellness, and Owyn caters to individuals seeking allergen-friendly, plant-based solutions.

The popularity of these TikTok beauty hashtags reflects a consumer preference for approachable, practical beauty solutions that fit seamlessly into daily routines. Minimalist trends like #SimpleNailDesigns and #GlowySkinMakeup emphasise a desire for natural-looking, effortless aesthetics. Hashtags such as #MatureMakeupLook and #HairRescue highlight the growing interest in age-inclusive beauty and targeted solutions for specific concerns, such as damaged hair. Meanwhile, #PressOnNailSets points to a demand for convenient, DIY beauty products that allow for personalisation and professional results at home.

It has been revealed that consumers are investing in bodycare. Their rising interest in products like glycolic body lotion, turmeric soap and glutathione cream suggests a consumer shift towards products that incorporate skincare-grade ingredients for targeted body benefits like exfoliation, brightening and antioxidant protection. More specifically, the popularity of body dry brushing points to a growing interest in selfcare rituals that improve skin texture and circulation. As for brands, heritage companies such as Head & Shoulders and Arm & Hammer highlight a consumer preference for functional solutions that address specific concerns such as odour control, whereas interest in Drunk Elephant and Zents reflects a growing inclination towards skin-friendly products that place emphasis on gentle formulation and sensory experience. Across the board, growth at L’Oréal Paris underscores the appeal of accessible products that blend efficacy with affordability.

Overall, more consumers are treating bodycare with the same level of customisation and sophistication as facial skincare, seeking products that deliver both functional and rejuvenating benefits that balance reliability and accessibility with a desire for elevated, skin-centric bodycare options, which meet both practical and experiential needs.

On TikTok, this week’s trending beauty hashtags reflect consumer interest in personalised routines, trending aesthetics and ingredient-led experimentation. #SkincareInOrder highlights the demand for education and clarity around effective skincare layering, while #AgeingSkinMakeup points to a focus on tailored beauty solutions for mature skin. The popularity of #PurpleBalayage and #HaileyBieberLipCombo showcases the influence of aspirational celebrity-driven trends and bold, expressive looks. Meanwhile, #TurmericScrubs illustrates the growing preference for plant-based, DIY and culturally rooted beauty remedies.

The top-growing fragrance trends show a strong consumer preference for unique, recognisable scent notes that align with a desire for familiar, comforting or refreshing elements. Scents like watermelon, vanilla and the more subdued earthy profile of matcha suggest a pull towards edible inspirations, with matcha offering a subtle alternative to classic gourmand scents. Discovery sets indicate a desire to explore without full commitment, showing curiosity around expanding fragrance profiles, and the importance of keeping consumers engaged and curious. As for fragrance brands, they reveal a consumer interest in personality-driven scents that blend classic appeal with modern influences. Brands such as Jean Paul Gaultier reflect a continued appreciation for iconic fragrances, while celebrity-backed lines from Melanie Martinez and Sabrina Carpenter cater to fans seeking identity-driven and relatable scent options. Also, Lattafa’s rise points to a growing fascination with Middle Eastern-inspired fragrances, bringing an element of luxury and cultural richness.

This week on TikTok, data reflects a consumer focus on durability, classic aesthetics and beauty solutions that deliver professional-grade results. Hashtags like #LonglastingLipColor and #BestConditioner suggest a preference for products that provide lasting performance, hinting at practicality and quality as top priorities. Classic styles like WhiteFrenchTips and #BlowoutHairstyles show a return to timeless, polished looks, indicating a desire for elegance and versatility in beauty routines. Meanwhile, #FullGlamMakeupTutorial emphasises a continued interest in mastering transformative techniques, revealing consumer enthusiasm for self-expression through bold, perfected beauty looks.

Industry observers note that when it comes to low-maintenance nailcare options, it’s their at-home application and offer of a quick, convenient nail fix that’s driving strong consumer desire. More specifically, semi-cured gel strips, bow nails and green chrome nails highlight an interest in creative self-expression, with playful designs and unique finishes that offer professional results without a salon visit; for bow nails, it’s the coquette trend prompting demand for the whimsical style. Nail growth serum and nail concealer reflect a growing focus on nail health and natural-looking aesthetics, indicating that consumers value functionality alongside beauty. Brands rising in line with such trends include Starrily, Dr Remedy, Mooncat, Dazzle Dry and Daisy DND, which together indicate a consumer shift towards high-quality, distinctive and health-conscious nailcare options.

They offer unique finishes — such as holographic, glitter and multi-chrome polishes from Starrily and Mooncat — catering to individuals seeking personalised and expressive nail aesthetics. Dazzle Dry’s focus on non-toxic, quick-drying and long-lasting formulas aligns with a growing preference for gentle options and more convenient at-home manicure solutions. These trends suggest that consumers want innovative products that merge aesthetic appeal with ease of use, prioritising accessible, customisable care. Additionally, the emphasis on vegan and cruelty-free products across these brands reflects an increasing consumer commitment to beauty practices perceived as ‘sustainable’.

According to recent reports, this week, the top-growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a growing consumer sentiment for hybrid products that bridge makeup and skincare, as seen through the #MakeupWithSkincare hashtag. Consumers also show a preference for soft, versatile aesthetics like #BabyPinkBlush and #BobKnotlessBraids, aligning with trends that feel effortless yet refined. Practicality is central, as #DryShampooTips and #HighlighterTutorial reflect a demand for easy-to-follow guidance, with users seeking tips and tutorials that offer convenient, effective beauty hacks. This trend illustrates a broader preference for DIY-style, educational content that enhances routines with minimal effort while helping achieve a desired look.

It has been revealed that this week’s top-growing makeup trends reflect a demand for long-wearing products that simplify routines while delivering lasting results. The preference for water-based and silicone-based foundations indicates that consumers are seeking products tailored to their specific skin types and needs — whether that be hydration and breathability from water-based options, or smoothness and longevity from silicone-based formulas. Peel-off lip tints and tubing mascaras highlight interest in transfer-resistant and enduring makeup products that withstand everyday life. Fixing sprays further demonstrate the desire for makeup longevity, reinforcing a theme of durability and convenience across all trends.

As for brands, Huda Beauty and Made by Mitchell appeal to those seeking vibrant, expressive makeup looks, while Dasique and McoBeauty cater to a desire for soft, natural aesthetics. Dasique also highlights the growing popularity of K-beauty brands in the makeup world. Mob Beauty, meanwhile, reflects growing a consumer interest in options perceived as sustainable without sacrificing quality. Overall, the makeup brands gaining traction suggest consumers are being drawn to bold, trend-driven products as well as minimal, everyday essentials.

It has been revealed that when it comes to TikTok this week, beauty consumers are actively seeking dramatic transformations and skincare rituals to enhance their everyday routines. #IcyEyes and #BigVolumeHair don’t only hark back to the noughties, but imply a desire for bold, eye-catching looks that amplify personal expression. In contrast, hashtags like #FaceSteaming and #GlycolicPads reflect a focus on contemporary skincare and selfcare practices that emphasise health and rejuvenation. The rise of #SkincareAdventCalendar underscores the appeal of curated, discovery-driven experiences, where consumers can explore new products in a fun and engaging way.

The top-growing skincare trends reflect a consumer focus on plant-based formulas and solutions that promise targeted results. Microneedle pimple patches, an innovation from regular pimple patches, offer deeper, more effective treatment for pimples and acne, while face taping taps into the desire for temporary anti-ageing effects by lifting and tightening the skin. Castor face oil, rice face masks and honey lip oil indicate a preference for nutrient-rich, plant-based remedies rooted in traditional beauty practices with hydrating and brightening properties. As for brands, Illiyoon and Beauty of Joseon underscore the influence of K-beauty, with a focus on calming, plant-based ingredients rooted in tradition, whereas Byoma represents a rising consumer focus on strengthening the skin’s barrier. YSL Beauty shows that luxury skincare remains highly sought after, appealing to those who prioritise both efficacy and brand prestige. Overall, consumers are increasingly gravitating towards products that balance efficacy with gentleness, emphasising skin health and barrier repair.

According to recent reports, among this week’s trending TikTok hashtags, there is an apparent consumer interest in enhancing natural beauty via techniques and products that deliver noticeable, polished results. Hashtags such as #FullLipsTutorial and #VoluminousBlowout emphasise the desire for amplified, voluminous looks, while #NaturalHairHack indicates a focus on embracing and enhancing natural hair textures. #BridalMakeupInspo reflects the importance of brands tapping into consumers’ life events. Meanwhile, #HydratingFoundation plays into the growing demand for makeup that not only enhances appearance, but also supports skin health through nourishing ingredients.

The rise in searches for scalp powders, pre-shampoos and scalp oiling indicates a growing consumer focus on scalp health and targeted care. Hair loss creams suggest that consumers are actively seeking solutions for hair thinning and plant-based treatments, with this trend overall reflecting an increasing preference for preemptive and restorative care routines whereby the scalp is considered an integral part of hair wellness. The top-growing haircare brands, like Hers and Act + Acre, highlight a consumer preference for clinically driven, treatment-focused products that prioritise hair health, particularly addressing concerns such as hair growth and scalpcare. Duke Cannon and Dr Squatch represent a shift towards grooming products often marketed to men that emphasise plant-based ingredients and rugged branding, while Gisou’s rise reflects the growing interest in products that care for the hair like hair oils and hair masks.

Overall, consumers are prioritising both preventative and recovery-oriented approaches in their haircare routines, with a noticeable lean toward multifunctional and plant-based remedies.

Recent findings suggest that the rise in hashtags like #HyaluronicAcidFillers and #GrowthOilForHair shows that consumers are deeply engaged with enhancing their appearances through clinical treatments and plant-based solutions. The popularity of #MensHairCutting highlights the increased attention to male grooming and personalised haircare trends, which is reflective of broader inclusivity across beauty content. Hashtags like #PamelaAndersonMakeup and #HalloweenLipGloss reveal a fascination with nostalgic and creative makeup looks, showcasing the playful and expressive side to beauty; however, Anderson’s no-makeup look is also driving growth for the hashtag.

According to recent reports, the trending supplement category is being driven by holistic wellness, with an emphasis on immunity, gut health and stress management. Supplement ingredients like colostrum and active hexose correlated compound (AHCC) highlight increased interest in immune-boosting ingredients, while magnesium oil and bergamot reflect a shift towards plant-based stress and mood regulation. Notably, sea moss ties into the growing popularity of nutrient-dense supplements. As for brand standouts, Armra Colostrum and Legendairy Milk indicate rising interest in immune support and maternal health. XWerks and Bodyhealth, meanwhile, reflect the focus on performance optimisation, particularly in fitness and recovery. Codeage appeals to a desire for comprehensive wellness, offering multi-functional supplements. Overall, the search data indicates that consumers are seeking multifunctional solutions to address both physical and mental well-being.

It has been revealed that consumers are seeking practical, problem-solving beauty solutions that fit seamlessly into their everyday lives. Hashtags such as #EasyHairHacks and #MakeupForGlasses highlight a preference for accessible, quick tips that enhance personal styling. #AcneSpecialist and #UnderArmBotox reflect rising interest in targeted treatments, with the latter signalling a shift in facial procedures like Botox as they move to the body for broader application. Additionally, the #FrenchBeauty hashtag references consumers looking to global beauty ideals for inspiration.

In a recent development, the top-growing bodycare trends reveal a consumer focus on ingredient-driven skincare products that address specific needs. Ingredients like turmeric and glutathione reflect a growing demand for offerings that have brightening and antioxidant properties, appealing to those seeking a solution to hyperpigmentation. Meanwhile, bodycare brand CLN Wash, addresses the needs of acne-prone and sensitive skin, reflecting a growing awareness of the importance of gentle, effective cleansing options. Retinol hand cream highlights an increasing interest in anti-ageing solutions, particularly for areas like the hands, which are often overlooked in skincare routines. As for brand standouts, Luna Daily focuses on microbiome-balancing formulations for all skin types, including intimate areas, showcasing a holistic approach to skin health, while Cocoapink’s commitment to plant-based ingredients resonates with a demand for gentle products that promote overall skin health without harsh chemicals.

It has been revealed that the fastest-rising beauty hashtags on TikTok reveal a dynamic shift in consumer preferences towards inclusive and personalised beauty experiences. #YellowBraids highlights a celebration of unique hairstyles and cultural expression, as well as a desire for individuality in beauty choices. The emergence of the #ManFacial signifies the increasing interest of male consumers in skincare and grooming. Meanwhile, hashtags such as #AcneProneMakeup and #GelMoisturiser underscore a growing focus on targeted solutions and textures for specific skin concerns. The #ScalpFacial hashtag ushers in the skinification of haircare, reflecting consumers’ desires for holistic approaches that prioritise both skin and hair health.

The top-growing fragrance trends in search data reveal a strong consumer preference for gourmand and comforting scents like vanilla, caramel, and watermelon, indicating a desire for sensory indulgence and familiarity, as well as more subdued edible scents like matcha. The rise in interest in discovery sets suggests consumers are becoming more experimental, seeking variety and personalisation in their fragrance choices while the popularity of body mists, which are lighter and more versatile than perfumes, indicates consumers' interest in layering scents for everyday wear. Notable top-growing brands include By Rosie Jane Lattafa and Sabrina Carpenter’s Sweet Tooth fragrance brand highlighting the appeal of niche fragrances and celebrity-backed scents. Overall, consumers are drawn to personal storytelling and the emotional connection tied to specific brands or figures.

Sources indicate that the top-growing beauty hashtags on TikTok this week suggest that consumers are seeking seasonal and therapeutic beauty experiences. Hashtags like #skincareadventcalendar and #falllippie highlight the appeal of season-specific products and rituals that tie beauty to key moments or holidays. #Skincaretherapy and #promakeuptip emphasise a desire for expert-driven tips and routines and the rise of #frecklemakeup shows how consumers are embracing creative self-expression through makeup trends.

Nail concealers and nail growth serums are among the main drivers for consumer interest within the nail space, reflecting the desire for both healthy nails and restorative care. Bow nails and green chrome nails, meanwhile, highlight the growing appeal of playful, bold nail designs as a means of personal expression. As for the category’s top-growing nail colours, Spate indicates pastel colours (+52.5 per cent year-on-year) and sheer finishes (+26.6 per cent year-on-year). Overall, these trends suggest that consumers are seeking a balance between nail care and artistic self-expression, blending practicality with creativity.

Recent findings suggest that the popularity of #GoingOutMakeupLook and #NoMakeupMakeupRoutine indicates that consumers are seeking bold, glam looks for social outings, alongside more subtle, natural styles for everyday wear; reflecting versatility in beauty preferences once again. #BlushTok remains strong as a trend that enhances consumer’s natural features using playful and exaggerated blush techniques. Elsewhere, #ItchyScalp is on the rise, signalling an increased consumer attention to scalp health, while #StraightBackBraids points to a growing interest in protective hairstyles that celebrate cultural identity and practical hair care.

According to recent reports, the top makeup trends suggest that consumers are increasingly prioritising long-lasting products in their beauty routines, as well as opting for products that allow for the creation of bold makeup looks. Tubing mascara and brow stain highlight a desire for smudge-proof, day-long wear, while duochrome eyeshadow and cluster lashes reflect an interest in multidimensional looks that stand out. Brands like Mob Beauty, Gressa and Tower 28 Beauty emphasise the demand for plant-based, skin-friendly formulations that appeal to consumers who value health-conscious beauty routines. Meanwhile, Devinah Cosmetics and Lethal Cosmetics cater to those seeking bold, artistic expression through vibrant, high-pigment colours and hues.

Industry observers note that when it comes to makeup concerns, there is a strong consumer focus on achieving a clear, smooth complexion while avoiding problems that could exacerbate various skin problems. Concerns about sebum and comedogenic products highlight a widespread desire to manage oil production and prevent clogged pores, indicating a need for non-irritating and breathable formulas. The focus on cakey makeup suggests that consumers are zooming in on how product texture and application impact the natural appearance of their skin.

Overall, these trends underscore a consumer inclination towards high-performance, visually impactful products that enhance and define key features.

It has been revealed that the growing interest in these skincare trends reflects a consumer shift towards plant-based formulas and DIY beauty routines. Consumers are increasingly drawn to ingredients with perceived holistic benefits, such as rice, honey and turmeric, indicating a preference for products that promise gentle and effective results. The emphasis on hydration, seen in trends like water-based cleansers, highlights a desire for clean, non-greasy solutions that maintain skin balance. Additionally, the rise of face taping suggests a growing interest in non-invasive techniques for achieving youthful skin and prioritising prevention.

The rising popularity of these skincare brands reflects a consumer preference for specialised, ingredient-focused products that cater to specific skin needs. Consumers are gravitating towards brands that emphasise science-backed formulations, as seen in Sebamed’s focus on pH balance and Byoma’s barrier-boosting ingredients. There’s also a growing appreciation for multicultural influences, with brands like Illiyoon and Sabbatical Beauty drawing from Korean skincare traditions, and Elaluz offering formulas with Brazilian superfoods.

The increasing focus on skincare concerns indicates a consumer shift towards addressing specific, often sensitive, skin complications. Consumers are becoming more aware of the underlying causes of skin problems, such as the impact of pore-clogging (comedogenic) ingredients and the influence of skin conditions like eczema and fungal acne. This trend suggests a growing demand for targeted treatments that are gentle, effective, and suitable for delicate areas like the eyelids. Additionally, the rise in searches for chin acne can be linked to lifestyle factors, such as mask-wearing and stress, as well as hormonal factors, driving consumers to seek solutions for these rising concerns.

Sources indicate that consumers are increasingly focused on scalp health and hair strength, as evidenced by the rising interest in scalp oiling and scalp serums. The popularity of hair loss topical solutions and rosemary shampoo reflects a preference for products that not only combat hair loss but also nourish and fortify the hair. The growing interest in low-porosity shampoo indicates a heightened awareness of individual hair needs and a desire for personalised care. Overall, these trends suggest a prioritisation in holistic haircare routines that enhance both scalp health and hair resilience.

Sources indicate that the top-growing haircare brands reflect a consumer shift towards products that prioritise formulations and solutions. Brands such as Seen, Gisou, and Act + Acre are gaining traction for their emphasis on scalp and hair health, highlighting a holistic approach to beauty that starts with the skin and scalp. Dr Squatch, meanwhile, underscores a demand for plant-based products that are often associated with masculine grooming. Pattern Beauty’s growth signals a focus on inclusivity and products tailored to specific hair types and curl patterns. Overall, these trends indicate a consumer preference for personalised and ingredient-driven haircare solutions.

Among the trending haircare ingredients lies a consumer preference for multi-functional components that offer both therapeutic and cosmetic benefits. Ingredients such as wild ginger, rosemary and eucalyptus reflect a demand for plant-based products that promote scalp health, stimulate hair growth and enhance overall hair vitality. The rising interest in jojoba highlights a trend towards deeply moisturising and nourishing formulas. The inclusion of ketoconazole, an antifungal agent, indicates that consumers are increasingly interested in more targeted treatments, particularly for conditions like dandruff or other fungal-related concerns. Overall, these trends suggest that consumers are gravitating towards ingredient-driven haircare solutions that blend traditional remedies with contemporary benefits.

In a recent development, the rise in active hexose correlated compound (AHCC) and rutin supplements indicates a focus on niche, immune-boosting and antioxidant-rich ingredients, while the demand for melatonin-free sleep aids suggests a shift towards non-hormonal alternatives for enhancing sleep, partly driven by concerns over long-term supplement use. Tower pilates are reflective of the trend towards low-impact yet effective exercise routines. Increased searches for magnesium oil highlight a preference for topical and targeted approaches to stress and muscle relaxation, aligning with the broader trend of holistic, multi-benefit wellness products.

Industry observers note that the trending wellness and supplement brands underscore a shift towards specialised wellness products that offer personalised benefits, resonating with consumers who are increasingly informed and selective in their wellness choices. For example, the growing interest in wellness brands like Winged Wellness and Pure Encapsulations reflects a consumer preference for targeted supplements that boast transparency and plant-based ingredients. XWERKS and Bodybio’s popularity also highlights a demand for performance-focused and bioavailable products, catering to consumers seeking optimal health and athletic performance. Bioray’s rise can be partly credited to a trend towards detoxification, aligning with a broader desire for holistic wellness solutions.

The rising search interest in ingredients such as colostrum and sea moss suggests a growing consumer focus on nutrient-dense supplements that support immune health and overall well-being. AHCC and rutin highlight ingredients that cater to targeted health concerns, such as immune system support and antioxidant benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of L-theanine indicates a desire for stress relief and cognitive support through plant-based, non-stimulant solutions.

Recent findings suggest that the search data for current bodycare trends reveals a consumer shift towards a ‘skinification’ of bodycare products, like turmeric soap and retinol hand cream, indicating a desire for comprehensive solutions that address specific concerns such as hyperpigmentation and anti-ageing. Interest in tallow soap, meanwhile, reflects a preference for hydrating and nourishing ingredients, whereas the popularity of peach body wash and vanilla body scrub underscores the importance of combining functionality, like cleansing and exfoliation, with pleasurable, aromatic experiences. Overall, consumers are seeking products that blend targeted skincare benefits with self-care rituals.

It has been revealed that consumers are revealing an increased preference for both heritage brands and product innovation in personal care. Summer’s Eve reflects the demand for specialised feminine hygiene solutions, while CO Bigelow’s growth points to an appreciation for apothecary traditions. Native’s rise showcases a trend towards affordable products that prioritise simplicity and effectiveness, and Saltair’s popularity indicates a growing interest in bodycare that incorporates active skincare ingredients and botanicals, blending nourishment with an elevated experience.

Ingredients addressing specific skin concerns while indulging in self-care are emerging. Turmeric’s popularity highlights a focus on targeting hyperpigmentation, while tallow reflects a growing demand for holistic ingredients that offer moisture and hydration. Peach and Tahitian vanilla suggest a desire for ingredients that combine skin benefits with indulgent and aromatic experiences. Sandalwood’s appeal points to an interest in soothing scents that enhance a holistic approach to bodycare.

Recent findings suggest that fragrance trends with the greatest prominence across search data all highlight a desire for convenient and versatile scent experiences. The popularity of perfume discovery sets and subscriptions indicates a lean toward exploration and variety, which allows consumers to try multiple scents without committing to full-size bottles. Meanwhile, oil-based perfumes and hair fragrances indicate a demand for long-lasting and multifunctional products that integrate seamlessly into daily routines, like fragrance layering, for example. The heightened interest in travel perfumes reinforces the need for portable and convenient products that cater to the on-the-go lifestyles of beauty consumers.

In a recent development, among the top-growing fragrance brands in search data, there is a clear consumer preference for both classic brands and more contemporary lines crafted by celebrities.
